review_comments.body:
🔶 **Bug** | Major

**Local-time getMonth misfiles payments near month ends.** `new Date(payment.created_at).getMonth()` uses the server's local timezone, but `created_at` and the `from`/`to` bounds are UTC. On a non-UTC host, a payment at 2026-01-31T23:30Z lands in February (UTC+1) or Dec 31 2026T23:30Z lands in January. The old code sliced the UTC string.

<details><summary>🤖 Fix with AI</summary>

```text
Fix this code review finding in GauravChopada/ledgerline, pull request 4. The line number is from commit 9577c7b; if the file has changed since, find the same code.

[Major] Local-time getMonth misfiles payments near month ends — src/routes/reports.ts:34
`new Date(payment.created_at).getMonth()` uses the server's local timezone, but `created_at` and the `from`/`to` bounds are UTC. On a non-UTC host, a payment at 2026-01-31T23:30Z lands in February (UTC+1) or Dec 31 2026T23:30Z lands in January. The old code sliced the UTC string.

Read the code at the location first and confirm the problem. Make the smallest change that fixes it, without changing unrelated code or existing behaviour. Add or update a test that would have caught it. If you think it is not a real problem, say why instead of changing the code.
```

</details>

🔶 **Bug** | Major

**Renamed customers keep showing old details.** customerSummary returns the cached entry with no expiry or invalidation, and PATCH /customers/:id in customers.ts never touches the cache. After a rename or email change, GET /invoices keeps returning the old name and email until the process restarts. Drop the cache and fetch the page's customers in one `WHERE id IN (...)` query.

<sub>Same root cause also at: `src/customer-cache.ts:8`</sub>

<details><summary>🤖 Fix with AI</summary>

```text
Fix this code review finding in GauravChopada/ledgerline, pull request 4. The line number is from commit 9577c7b; if the file has changed since, find the same code.

[Major] Renamed customers keep showing old details — src/customer-cache.ts:13
customerSummary returns the cached entry with no expiry or invalidation, and PATCH /customers/:id in customers.ts never touches the cache. After a rename or email change, GET /invoices keeps returning the old name and email until the process restarts. Drop the cache and fetch the page's customers in one `WHERE id IN (...)` query.

Read the code at the location first and confirm the problem. Make the smallest change that fixes it, without changing unrelated code or existing behaviour. Add or update a test that would have caught it. If you think it is not a real problem, say why instead of changing the code.
```

</details>

🔶 **Bug** | Major

**Revenue rows reordered from month-first to currency-first.** The response is now sorted by currency and then month. Before, rows came in chronological order (Jan USD, Jan EUR, Feb USD). A client reading rows as a time series breaks, and the description does not mention the reorder. A currency with no payments in the year is also missing, so an empty year returns `rows: []` and the chart still can't plot directly.

<details><summary>🤖 Fix with AI</summary>

```text
Fix this code review finding in GauravChopada/ledgerline, pull request 4. The line number is from commit 9577c7b; if the file has changed since, find the same code.

[Major] Revenue rows reordered from month-first to currency-first — src/routes/reports.ts:40
The response is now sorted by currency and then month. Before, rows came in chronological order (Jan USD, Jan EUR, Feb USD). A client reading rows as a time series breaks, and the description does not mention the reorder. A currency with no payments in the year is also missing, so an empty year returns `rows: []` and the chart still can't plot directly.

Read the code at the location first and confirm the problem. Make the smallest change that fixes it, without changing unrelated code or existing behaviour. Add or update a test that would have caught it. If you think it is not a real problem, say why instead of changing the code.
```

</details>
Separate from staleness: is there any memory risk in this cache for a long-running, multi-tenant server?

Yes — the Map never evicts entries, so in a long-running multi-tenant process it grows unbounded with every distinct tenantId:customerId pair ever looked up, which is an unbounded memory leak on top of the staleness issue. That's another reason to drop the cache in favor of the batched query.

output.summary: Adds an in-memory customer-cache module to embed customer summaries (id/name/email) into the /invoices list response, and reworks /reports/revenue to join payments with invoices in a single query, grouping by currency and emitting all 12 months per currency instead of only months with activity. Includes tests for the new invoice customer embedding and the revenue report's full-year output.
